excerpt: "Netscape time" once meant moving fast to genuinely innovate. Turned loose on growth for its own sake, the same speed hollows companies out.
summary: Jay Hoffmann revisits "Netscape time," the culture of breakneck development that defined the early web, and traces what happens when that pace is aimed at growth rather than at building something good. Following the pattern through companies like Yahoo, Mozilla, and Spotify, he argues the industry keeps facing the same fork: serve users and build something worth keeping, or chase growth metrics until the product bloats and loses its focus. The lesson he lands on is simple and durable: build something people love, and build revenue to keep it sustainable.
title: Thinking More About Netscape Time
